correctness.rationale: Re-audited the repaired theorem. On each stable color class, the sum L_j of absolute weights is bounded by width w, and the squared mass Q_j is at most L_j². The color-class deficits d_j=w²−Q_j sum to δ. The peak m_j satisfies Q_j≤m_j w, so both its deficit from w and the entire off-peak L1 mass are ≤d_j/w. This gives squared error ≤2d_j²/w² per class when replacing the peak by signed w and zeroing the tail. The alternative off-peak squared bound Q_j−m_j²≤Q_j(1−Q_j/w²)≤d_j independently gives the frozen estimate, justifying the minimum of the two. At the strict threshold δ<w², each pair of peaks has total magnitude >w, ruling out opposite signs by singleton supports and same-sign nonedges by a stable pair. For q=1 the peak is automatically nonzero and no pair condition is needed. The final normalization costs precisely √q(w−1/√q). The exact clique width and minimizers follow at δ=0. The complete-graph perturbation and the two-vertex edgeless perturbation have both distance and deficit asymptotically proportional to the perturbation parameter, so no o(δ) uniform rate is possible at fixed q. The repaired result's polar comparison follows by taking the zero-height section and maximizing projected norm, not by identifying an ordinary inradius with width.
residual_risks: The frozen 810-graph consistency check does not verify the repaired sharper estimate; the latter is analytic. Constants and sufficiency threshold are not claimed optimal.

evidence: The Hansen zero-height slice is (K−K)/2. Projecting its polar gives points x with squared norm ≤2(1+t²)μ≤4μ, where t is the original polar height and μ is the maximum squared norm over Q. Equality forces t=±1 and projected points are signed doubled maximizers of Q. A q-coloring bounds μ≤q and equality requires one unit coordinate per class forming a maximum clique.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This recovers width 1/√q and all signed clique normals without the frozen proof. It does not give the repaired stability rate. The new linear control uses the residual absolute mass per class, recovery of a coherent clique under the strict threshold and a sharpness family; it is not a restatement of the exact polar maximizer formula.

value.rationale: On a natural class wider than perfect graphs, the repaired theorem recovers a specific signed maximum clique from an almost thinnest direction, with a distance bound independent of graph order and optimal linear order in the small deficit at fixed q. Compactness for any fixed polytope gives neither a uniform constant nor this rate. The specialization also controls approximate recovery of longest chains.
residual_risks: No theorem for χ>ω or an optimal coefficient in the stability estimate is claimed.
